name: Incline Dumbbell Row
description: The incline dumbbell row is performed lying prone on an incline bench, allowing each arm to row freely from a fully extended position. The incline angle shifts emphasis toward the upper back and rear deltoids relative to flat or horizontal rows, while the bench support reduces lower back fatigue and allows higher quality reps later in a training session.

execution.starting_position: Set a bench to a low incline of approximately 30 degrees. Lie prone on the bench with the chest supported and feet on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with arms hanging below the bench.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the adjustable bench to a 30-degree incline. Use lighter dumbbells than you would use for a bent-over row since the range of motion is longer from this position.
steps: Step 1: Begin with arms hanging straight down, fully extended.
Step 2: Row both dumbbells simultaneously toward the waist by driving the elbows up and back.
Step 3: Retract the shoulder blades at the top of the movement.
Step 4: Lower the dumbbells slowly to full arm extension, allowing the shoulder blades to protract.
Step 5: Repeat without letting momentum take over.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you row up. Inhale as you lower the dumbbells.
common_mistakes: Setting the bench too steep, which changes the movement pattern significantly
Short repping at the bottom and not achieving full scapular protraction
Internally rotating the shoulders by rowing with palms facing backward
safety_considerations: Keep the head neutral — do not crane the neck upward
Ensure the bench is on a stable, non-slip surface
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Maximize scapular protraction at the bottom and retraction at the top.
coaching_cues: Lead with the elbows, not the hands
Think of pulling your shoulder blades into your back pockets
